verdict.rationale: Asking whether an operating system's settings and functions can be driven programmatically is a fair question for Windows, so the axis applies. The only relevant evidence is a probe pointing to official PowerShell scripting documentation, a first-party programmatic surface for the OS, though nothing shows it reaches parity with the UI. The Windows App SDK and WinUI items are building blocks for writing apps rather than a way to control what the UI does, so they earn no credit. Missing for 10: any documented claim of UI-to-API/CLI parity, coverage of specific UI features (Settings, Snap, account setup) via the programmatic interface, an OS-level automation API reference, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
